entries.title: Campaign worktrees must propagate their environment
entries.guidance: Load the isolated campaign worktree environment before build and server startup, pass it to both child processes, and preserve explicit process values.

evidence.summary: Actual planning requests failed because the isolated campaign worktree environment was not loaded into the build and server child processes. The durable campaign-runner fix loads the worktree environment and passes it to both processes while preserving explicit process values.

entries.title: Moving owned objects need position-following target checks
entries.guidance: Query targets around the owned object current observed position on bounded recurring lifecycle checks shorter than its lifetime; reschedule while active and stop after the first hit or expiry.

evidence.summary: Actual source generation repeatedly produced a transient projectile that traveled and was cleaned up but queried and mutated the target at its stationary location immediately after creation, before the owned object could overlap the target. The durable source-generation prompt now requires target queries to follow the owned object's current observed position during scheduled or fixed-step travel, with bounded rescheduling and cleanup after the first hit or expiry.

The source repair preserved owned-object creation, actor origin, travel, and active state, but scheduled the first target query at the full projectile lifetime. The moving object passed the target between observations and targetInteractionsDelta remained zero. The durable mechanic-general source guidance now requires bounded recurring lifecycle checks shorter than the accepted lifetime, with active travel and rescheduling before expiry until the target is reached.

entries.title: Active owned objects must survive post-action observation
entries.guidance: Keep active owned objects observable through the post-action lifecycle check and defer expiry cleanup until after bounded motion and target interaction can be observed.

evidence.summary: Actual source generation created and moved an owned projectile, interacted with the target, and then destroyed it before the post-action observation. The durable mechanic-general source-generation repair guidance now requires active owned objects to remain observable through the post-action lifecycle check, with bounded motion, target interaction, and deferred expiry cleanup.

entries.title: Negative timestamp sentinels must permit the first action
entries.guidance: When a last-action timestamp uses a negative sentinel for no prior action, bypass cooldown on the first accepted action and write the current time only after acceptance.

evidence.summary: The source repair rejected the first logical action because it compared simulation time against a negative initial last-action sentinel as if a prior action existed. The accepted contract initializes last_fire_time_ms to -1, so the first action must bypass cooldown and write the current time only after acceptance. The durable mechanic-general timestamp guidance now makes that sentinel rule explicit and adds it to zero-creation lifecycle repair diagnosis.

entries.title: Spatial queries must use accepted target-kind provenance
entries.guidance: Use the exact runtime object kind from the accepted target binding in spatial queries; never substitute a binding ID or invent an object-kind string.

evidence.summary: The source repair created, moved, and cleaned up the projectile but queried an invented target object kind instead of the accepted runtime kind of the bound target. The durable mechanic-general source guidance now requires exact target-kind provenance from the accepted target binding and forbids binding IDs or invented object-kind strings in spatial queries.

entries.title: Preserve causal runtime errors across broker closure
entries.guidance: When authenticated runtime failure and Worker or broker closure arrive on separate channels, give the authenticated failure a bounded precedence window before emitting generic closure while retaining a fail-closed fallback.

evidence.summary: Authenticated causal runtime errors and remote Worker closure arrive on separate channels; immediate broker-closure failure could mask the queued causal error. Deferring generic closure handling one browser task preserves structured mechanic-general failure evidence while retaining fail-closed behavior.

The zero-delay broker-close fallback could still outrun an authenticated fatal runtime event delivered on a later browser task, leaving first-playable evidence with only the generic Worker-close message. A bounded 100 millisecond grace lets the causal runtime event terminate immediately when present while preserving automatic fail-closed handling for a genuine broker-only closure.

entries.title: Separate heartbeat and candidate execution budgets
entries.guidance: Keep candidate execution and termination bounds exact, but size the host heartbeat allowance for healthy browser scheduling delays and require causal runtime evidence before classifying a missed heartbeat as candidate failure.

evidence.summary: The browser-attested realm candidate completed its first capability probe, but the runtime heartbeat missed a 50 millisecond scheduling allowance without any browser or runtime error. Earlier campaigns passed the same gate, so the fixed heartbeat policy was too narrow for a healthy but briefly delayed browser task. Increasing only the host-heartbeat allowance to 250 milliseconds preserves the 50 millisecond candidate execution and termination bounds.

entries.title: Attach target proof to cleanup-capable scenarios
entries.guidance: For transient owned-object behavior, attach and verify required target-interaction proof only on time-advancing scenarios that explicitly declare cleanup with owned_object_count equals 0 or at_most 0. A scenario with no owned-object-count assertion is not cleanup-capable. Use the first time-advancing scenario only when no explicit cleanup scenario exists, and keep evaluator authoring and downstream verification aligned to that policy.

evidence.summary: Evaluator-authored target-interaction proof contradicted an early active-progress scenario while the accepted behavior destroyed the transient object on interaction.

Evaluator-authored target-interaction proof was applied to every time-advancing transient lifecycle scenario. Target proof now attaches to cleanup-capable scenarios, with the first time-advancing scenario retained as a fallback when no cleanup scenario exists.

An accepted repaired source produced an authentic passed deterministic-evaluation receipt, but handoff rejected it because active-progress evidence omitted target interaction while cleanup scenarios carried that proof.

The evaluator required target interaction on both the explicit zero-count cleanup scenario and a separate 100 ms travel scenario with no owned-object-count assertion. The travel scenario observed active creation and 36 units of motion but correctly had zero target interactions, exhausting all four source attempts against the misapplied proof.

The accepted cycle-10 contract correctly used a dispatch-only scenario for positive creation, but also declared projectile_travels_before_cleanup with dispatch_action, 100ms of advance_time, and a positive final owned_object_count. The initial and first repair source candidates both created at actor origin, traveled 70 units, recorded one target interaction, and destroyed the projectile during that advance, producing the valid final count 0 while the contract required at least 1. Later source repairs drifted to zero interactions, so the terminal attempt summary was downstream repair noise rather than the durable cause. KF-0008 and KF-0009 directly govern this contradiction: target proof belongs on cleanup-capable time-advancing scenarios, while positive transient creation proof must remain dispatch-only. The provider had ignored those existing prompt rules, and contract admission only rejected positive counts at or beyond the accepted lifetime. KF-0002, KF-0003, and KF-0005 govern the recurring target-check implementation but were satisfied by the earlier candidates' observed travel and interaction. KF-0011's deterministic geometry was reachable. KF-0004 and KF-0018's cooldown state guidance produced no state failure. KF-0014 did not govern this owned-object count, and KF-0017's callback checklist remained intact. The durable mechanic-general fix makes contract validation reject every positive transient owned-object count after any time advance while retaining the more specific post-lifetime diagnostic.

entries.title: Align deterministic and runtime targets with the actor proof path
entries.guidance: For finite-lifetime moving owned objects that must interact with a target, align both deterministic proof placement and returned Game Spec spawn geometry with the actor proof path. The declared speed multiplied by lifetime must exceed actor-to-target spawn-center distance with bounded interaction headroom, or a compatible target spawn must move nearer. Do not rely on deterministic target relocation, unrelated target movement, or source behavior outside the declared travel budget.

evidence.summary: The generated behavior created and traveled an active object but recorded zero target interactions because the deterministic target was off the accepted proof path.
Exact intent targets are now placed ahead of the first exact actor on the deterministic proof path; unrelated entity positions are unchanged.

The returned Game Spec spawned the player at center (105, 300) and enemy at center (660, 300), 555 pixels apart, while the accepted intent bounded projectile travel to 320 pixels per second for 900 milliseconds, or 288 pixels. Deterministic evaluation passed only because its fixture relocated the target to 32 pixels ahead of the actor; mounted first-playable cleanup then reported zero target interactions.

KF-0006, KF-0008, KF-0009, KF-0010, KF-0011, and KF-0012 were the complete applicable finding set, with no related findings. The actual candidate passed source generation and deterministic evaluation, where the target fixture was placed 32 pixels ahead of the actor, but failed first-playable in the returned runtime layout. The player spawn center was (105, 300) and the enemy spawn center was (660, 300), a 555-pixel separation, while the accepted intent bounded projectile travel to 320 pixels per second for 900 milliseconds, or 288 pixels. The source therefore created at the actor, moved, and cleaned up correctly but could not possibly reach the live target. The durable planning fix requires the combined Game Spec and Mechanic Intent to make finite-lifetime target travel mutually reachable: declared speed multiplied by lifetime must exceed actor-to-target spawn-center distance with at least 64 pixels of interaction headroom, or the compatible target spawn must move nearer. The append-only reconciliation extends KF-0011 from deterministic placement through planning and first-playable runtime geometry.

When the control checkout does not yet contain an accepted runner fix, invoke the accepted worktree CLI with --state-root pointing to the control checkout so application and harness code use the accepted revision while campaign evidence remains in the original persisted store. entries.title: Callback repairs must preserve the exact lifecycle checklist
entries.guidance: Treat the contract-derived required callback checklist as a closed set during initial generation and repair. evidence.summary: Source candidate callback kind "fixed_step" must occur exactly once and be declared by the accepted contract.

The accepted contract set fixedStep false and its exact required callback checklist excluded fixed_step. The initial actual source candidate respected that callback set but used ungranted state_read; all three actual repair candidates then added and retained an undeclared no-op fixed_step callback. The generic source prompt simultaneously rendered the exact closed checklist and an unconditional instruction to keep fixed_step minimal whenever scheduled callbacks implemented lifecycle behavior, while callback_coverage_mismatch repair lacked an explicit remove-when-undeclared rule. The durable fix qualifies fixed_step guidance by the exact contract-derived checklist and tells callback repair to remove undeclared kinds, add missing required kinds, and retain exactly one of each required kind without weakening validation.

entries.title: Post-action state observations must reflect accepted writes
entries.guidance: After an accepted action writes private state, final state observations must match that write or a later write caused by an explicit reachable callback. Advancing beyond a *_until deadline changes admission because the deadline is elapsed but does not reset the stored deadline to its initial sentinel; omit that final state assertion or assert the deterministic written value unless accepted behavior explicitly resets it.

evidence.summary: Model-declared observation 1 "state_equals" failed. Assertion: {"kind":"state_equals","stateId":"cooldown_until","value":-1}. Actual: 250.

The actual cycle-9 contract declared cooldown_until with initial sentinel -1, dispatched the accepted fire action, advanced time, and then required a final state_equals value of -1. Every actual source candidate preserved the exact accepted callback checklist and wrote a cooldown deadline after the accepted action; the observed value was 250, and no accepted reachable callback reset that state. The contract therefore contradicted its own accepted action semantics by requiring the pre-action sentinel after the action had deterministically updated the state. KF-0004 directly governs the negative sentinel and requires the first action to be admitted before writing the current timestamp, so it confirms that -1 is a pre-action state rather than a valid post-action assertion. KF-0017 is confirmed because cycle-9 source candidates preserved the closed callback checklist. KF-0002, KF-0003, KF-0005, KF-0008, KF-0009, KF-0011, and KF-0014 were also applicable to the classified projectile attempt but govern owned-object lifecycle, target provenance, evidence placement, geometry, or bound-object authority rather than this private-state observation. The durable mechanic-general fix requires post-action state observations to reflect accepted writes or explicit reachable resets and states that advancing beyond a *_until deadline does not reset its stored value to the initial sentinel.
Model-declared observation 2 "state_equals" failed. Assertion: {"kind":"state_equals","stateId":"cooldown_until","value":-1}. Actual: 400.

KF-0018 directly governed the failure: the accepted repaired contract established cooldown_until = 400 after fire_action in a dispatch-only scenario, then required the same action path to end at the initial -1 sentinel in three time-advancing scenarios. All four actual source attempts wrote 400 and failed those same contract-owned observations, confirming KF-0018 across a second independent campaign. KF-0004 confirms that a negative deadline sentinel permits the first action and is replaced only after acceptance. KF-0017's exact callback checklist was satisfied, and the KF-0020 trusted observation boundary from fix cycle 1 worked because evaluation read the actual value without widening source authority. KF-0002, KF-0003, KF-0005, KF-0008, KF-0009, KF-0011, and KF-0014 governed secondary projectile motion, target, evidence, geometry, cleanup, and bound-object observations but did not explain the repeated deadline mismatch. There were no related findings and no isolation was needed. The durable mechanic-general fix rejects only a witnessed *_until contradiction: a dispatch-only scenario must prove the same action writes a noninitial deadline before a time-advancing scenario with the same initial setup can be rejected for requiring the initial sentinel again.

Compile authenticated admitted callback source before active-work measurement while retaining compilation inside the bounded outer execution deadline. evidence.summary: Cycle 11 proved the cycle-11 contract fix worked: the initial time-advancing positive count was rejected, contract repair was accepted, the initial actual source passed deterministic evaluation, and Final Game Spec assembly succeeded.
